title: Tell part-to-part ratios from part-to-whole ratios

lesson.title: Part-to-Part or Part-to-Whole?

steps.say: You already know how to write a ratio to compare two things, like three to two. Today we learn something important: a ratio can compare one part to another part, or it can compare one part to the whole group. Knowing which one you are looking at is the whole trick.

Here is a bag of marbles from the toy shop on Main Street. There are three red marbles and two blue marbles. Look at the bar picture: the red bar is three units long, and the blue bar is two units long. Comparing red to blue, red to blue is three to two. That is a part compared to another part, so we call it a part to part ratio.

visual.caption: Red 3 and Blue 2 side by side: part to part is 3 to 2

steps.say: Now push the two bars together to make one long bar. Three red plus two blue makes five marbles all together. That five is the whole bag. So red compared to the whole bag is three to five. That is a part compared to the whole, so we call it a part to whole ratio. Same marbles, different comparison.

visual.caption: Red 3, Blue 2, and the whole bag 5: part to whole is 3 to 5

steps.say: Here is the mistake almost everyone makes. Someone sees three red and two blue and says, red is three halves of the bag. Stop and think! Three halves is more than one whole bag, and red is only part of the bag, so that cannot be right. The number two is only the blue part, not the whole. The whole is five. Red is three fifths of the bag, and three fifths is less than one whole. Whenever you say what fraction of the group something is, the bottom number must be the total.

visual.caption: Red is 3 out of the 5 marbles in the whole bag: three fifths

steps.say: Let's try one more together. A soccer team at recess has four girls and six boys. Four to six compares girls to boys, so that is part to part. Now add them: four plus six is ten players in the whole team. So girls to the whole team is four to ten. If someone asked what part of the team is girls, the answer is four tenths, not four sixths, because ten is the whole team.
steps.math: 4 : 6 \text{ part to part}, \quad 4 : 10 \text{ part to whole}

steps.say: So remember this: part to part compares one group with the other group, and part to whole compares one group with everybody added together. Before you write a ratio, always ask yourself, am I comparing to the other part, or to the whole?

lesson.answer: Part to part compares one part with the other part; part to whole compares one part with everything added together — so always ask yourself which one you need.

practice.question: Ms. Yuanyuan buys fruit at the Vancouver market: five apples and three pears. Draw a bar three units long for the pears and a bar five units long for the apples, then put them together to make the whole bar. First, write the part to part ratio of apples to pears. Then write the part to whole ratio of apples to all the fruit. Last, finish this sentence: apples are what fraction of all the fruit?
practice.answer: Apples to pears is five to three, a part to part ratio. All the fruit together is five plus three, which is eight, so apples to all the fruit is five to eight, a part to whole ratio. Apples are five eighths of all the fruit — not five thirds, because eight is the whole.
